title: The smooth dualizing object is the Tate twist
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, in the domain of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth,
separated, of pure
relative dimension $d$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

proof.text: Put $W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], $p_1$ is smooth and its diagonal section invariant has the base-change identification $\alpha:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_f$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion], $\Delta$ is a closed immersion and its normal bundle is canonically $N_{\Delta/W}\cong T_{X/Y}$. By [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free], $\Omega^1_{X/Y}$ is locally free of rank $d$. On an open where it is $\mathcal O_X^d$, its dual is $\mathcal O_X^d$ with the dual basis, so the relative tangent bundle has rank $d$, also when $d=0$. The equality $p_1\Delta=\mathrm{id}_X$ is the fibre-product diagonal identity. Thus $(p_1,\Delta)$ is a smooth morphism with a closed section, as required in [def-pur-section-invariant]. Only the closed-immersion and normal-bundle clauses of the geometry lemma are needed here, not a codimension convention excluding zero.

source.place: Proof, Step 1 of the unit sk-thm-smooth-purity; item Proof, Step 1 (diagonal and normal bundle), with the rank check from Stacks Tag 02G1, lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free

proof.text: Use the deformation family of [def-pur-dnc-section-family] for $g=p_1$, $s=\Delta$ and base $B=X$. Applying [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] gives the normalized isomorphism $\delta:C(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_T,0_T)$, where $\pi_T:T_{X/Y}\to X$. This uses the actual normal bundle identified in Step 1; no trivialization of $T_{X/Y}$ is selected and the bundle is not replaced by $\mathbf A^d_X$. The uniqueness and coordinate normalization in the cited theorem specify $\delta$ independently of the local coordinates.

source.place: Proof, Step 1 (deformation of the diagonal); unit sk-thm-smooth-purity Proof, Step 2

proof.text: Apply the explicitly stated dualizing-object clause of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] to the rank-$d$ bundle $\pi_T$. It gives a canonical $\gamma:\omega_{\pi_T}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{T_{X/Y}}(d)[2d]$. By [def-pur-section-invariant], $C(\pi_T,0_T)=L0_T^*\omega_{\pi_T}$. The schemes $X$ and $T_{X/Y}$ are in the separated finite-type setting of vector-bundle purity: the vector-bundle projection is affine by its relative-Spec description, and on a trivializing affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ its total space is $\operatorname{Spec}R[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$. Thus the projection is separated and of finite type, and its composite with the separated finite-type map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ has both properties. The zero section is the closed immersion defined by the augmentation in [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Apply the functor $L0_T^*$ to $\gamma$ and then use the explicit restriction clause of [lem-pur-immersion-twist]: the restriction of $\Lambda_{T_{X/Y}}(d)[2d]$ to the closed zero section is $\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$. This yields $\beta:C(\pi_T,0_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$. The citation of the immersion lemma is solely to its stated restriction identification; no identification of $L0_T^*$ with $R0_T^!$ is made and its exceptional-pullback formula is not applied.

source.place: Proof, Step 2 (vector-bundle purity and zero-section restriction); unit sk-thm-smooth-purity Proof, Step 3

proof.text: Define $\theta_f=\beta\circ\delta\circ\alpha^{-1}:\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ using the three isomorphisms constructed above. Its inverse is $\alpha\circ\delta^{-1}\circ\beta^{-1}$: the two composites cancel successive inverse pairs. The arrows $\alpha$ (the specified base-change comparison), $\delta$ (the uniquely normalized deformation comparison), and $\beta$ (the canonical vector-bundle comparison followed by coefficient restriction) were specified without choices. Their composite is therefore the claimed canonical isomorphism. This is a construction of the specified map, not a claim that all isomorphisms between these two objects are equal.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions],
let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth,
separated, of pure
relative dimension $d$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

proof.text:
The final restriction of the Tate line uses [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with tensor identifications as in [def-weil-derived-tensor].
Step 1: the section invariant of the diagonal. Apply
[thm-pur-dnc-invariance] to the smooth map
$p_1:W\to X$ of [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] and its closed
section $\Delta$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion] its
normal bundle is canonically $N_\Delta\cong T_{X/Y}$, a vector
bundle of rank $d$, so

$$
C(p_1,\Delta)\;\cong\;C(\pi_T:T_{X/Y}\to X,\,0_T).
$$

Step 2: the two sides. The left side is $\omega_f$ by
[lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]. For the right side,
[cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] applied to $\pi_T$ gives

$$
\omega_{\pi_T}=R\pi_T^!\Lambda_X\;\cong\;\Lambda_{T_{X/Y}}(d)[2d],
$$

and pulling back by the zero section $0_T$ gives

$$
C(\pi_T,0_T)=0_T^*\omega_{\pi_T}
\;\cong\;0_T^*\Lambda_{T_{X/Y}}(d)[2d]
\;\cong\;\Lambda_X(d)[2d].
$$

Combining the two steps proves the assertion. The identification is
canonical (every displayed step is canonical, by the uniqueness clause
of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]); compatibility with base change
follows from the base-change compatibility of the diagonal, of
[thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and of
[cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] (the normal bundle of the diagonal
of the base change is the base change of the normal bundle).
